concrete.metaTitle: Concrete Calculator — Slab & Concrete Yard Calculator | BuildCalc
concrete.metaDescription: Free concrete calculator, concrete slab calculator, and concrete yard calculator. Estimate cubic yards, cubic meters, waste, and premixed bags.
concrete.intro: Use this concrete calculator to estimate cubic yards (yd³), cubic meters (m³), and premixed bags for rectangular slabs, footings, and cylindrical columns—with waste allowance and step-by-step math.

fields.wasteHelp: Recommended: 5%–10% for slabs; 10%–15% for uneven ground.
fields.bagHelp: Optional: estimates how many premixed concrete bags you need.

guide.title: What this concrete calculator is for and how to use it
guide.purpose: Whether you need a concrete slab calculator for a patio or driveway, or a concrete yard calculator to order ready-mix delivery, this tool computes exact volume in cubic yards (yd³), cubic feet (ft³), and cubic meters (m³) before you buy.
guide.howTitle: How to use it step by step
steps: Choose your unit system: Imperial (feet and inches, outputting yd³ and ft³) or Metric (meters and centimeters, outputting m³).
Select the element shape: Rectangular slab or footing, or Cylindrical column or pier.
Enter the dimensions (length, width, and thickness for slabs; diameter and height for columns) plus the quantity of identical elements.
Set a waste allowance percentage (5%–10% is standard for formed slabs; 10%–15% for uneven subgrades or footings).
Optionally choose a premixed bag size (40 lb, 60 lb, 80 lb, 25 kg, or 50 kg) to see the rounded-up bag count.

formula.title: Formula, units, and waste calculation
equations: Slab or footing: V = Length × Width × Thickness × Quantity
Cylindrical column: V = π × (Diameter / 2)² × Height × Quantity
formula.p1: Units and conversions: in Imperial mode, thickness is entered in inches and divided by 12 to convert to feet; cubic feet are divided by 27 to get cubic yards (1 yd³ = 27 ft³). In Metric mode, thickness or diameter in centimeters is divided by 100 to convert to meters.
formula.p2: For cylindrical columns or piers, the circular cross-section area π × r² is multiplied by height and quantity.
formula.p3: Material waste: adding 5%–10% waste compensates for uneven subgrades, formwork deflection, compaction, and concrete left in wheelbarrows or pump lines.
formula.p4: Premixed bags divide total volume by standard manufacturer yield (for example, ~0.60 ft³ per 80 lb bag, ~0.45 ft³ per 60 lb bag, or ~0.022 m³ per 50 kg bag), rounded up to whole bags.

interpret.title: How to interpret the results
items: Net volume: exact geometric volume without any loss allowance.
Total volume (with waste): the volume to order from a ready-mix supplier or use for bag calculations.
Equivalent: shows the same volume in cubic feet or cubic yards for easy comparison.
Bags needed: whole number of premixed bags rounded up to cover the total volume.

items.title: 10 × 10 ft slab at 4 in thick
items.scenario: A standard 10 ft by 10 ft patio slab, 4 inches (0.333 ft) thick, with 10% waste.
items.result: Result: 1.358 yd³ total (or 62 bags of 80 lb).

items.title: 5 × 4 m slab at 10 cm thick
items.scenario: A 5 m × 4 m slab, 10 cm (0.10 m) thick, with 10% waste.
items.result: Result: 2.20 m³ of concrete (or 100 bags of 50 kg).

faq.q: How much concrete do I need for a 10 m² slab?
faq.a: At 10 cm (0.10 m) thickness, a 10 m² slab needs 1.00 m³ net (1.10 m³ with 10% waste). At 12 cm thickness, it needs 1.20 m³ net (1.32 m³ with 10% waste).

faq.q: How many 80 lb bags are in a cubic yard of concrete?
faq.a: One 80 lb premixed bag yields about 0.60 ft³, so 1 cubic yard (27 ft³) requires approximately 45 bags of 80 lb.

faq.q: What waste percentage should I add?
faq.a: For formed slabs on a level base, 5%–10% is usually enough. For rough ground excavations or irregular footings, use 10%–15%.

faq.q: Does this work for mortar or pure cement bags?
faq.a: Volume (yd³ / m³) applies to any pour, but the bag count assumes premixed concrete bags (with aggregate included), not pure Portland cement.

faq.q: Do I need to convert inches to feet manually?
faq.a: No. In imperial mode, thickness is entered directly in inches (in) and converted to feet automatically.

paint.metaDescription: Calculate how many gallons or liters of paint you need based on room size, ceiling, coats, coverage and openings. Instant results.
paint.intro: Estimate gallons or liters of paint for walls and ceilings, subtracting doors and windows and rounding up by container size.

fields.doorsHelp: Standard deduction: ~20 ft² (1.85 m²) per door.
fields.windowsHelp: Standard deduction: ~15 ft² (1.40 m²) per window.
fields.coverageHelp: Typical: 350–400 ft²/gal (10–12 m²/L). Check the can label.

results.openingsClamped: Opening deductions exceeded wall area and were clamped to 0.
results.openingsWarning: Openings exceed the given area: check your measurements.

guide.title: What this paint coverage calculator is for and how to use it
guide.purpose: Whether you need a wall paint calculator for a single room, a ceiling paint calculator, or a full room paint calculator, this tool estimates how much paint you need before you buy.
guide.howTitle: How to use it step by step
steps: Choose between entering room dimensions (length, width, wall height) or total surface area directly.
Check 'Include ceiling' if you are painting the ceiling with the same paint, and enter the number of doors and windows to subtract.
Set the number of coats (2 coats is standard) and the coverage per coat from your paint can (default: 350 ft²/gal in Imperial or 10 m²/L in Metric).
Add a waste allowance (5%–10% for roller absorption and touch-ups).
Select a container size (1 qt, 1 gal, 5 gal, 1 L, 4 L, 10 L, or 20 L) to see the rounded-up can count.

formula.title: Formula and calculation criteria
formula.p1: Room perimeter is multiplied by wall height to get gross wall area. If ceiling is checked, Length × Width is added.
formula.p2: Standard opening deductions (20 ft² / 1.85 m² per door and 15 ft² / 1.40 m² per window) are subtracted.
formula.p3: Net area is multiplied by the number of coats and divided by single-coat coverage.
formula.p4: Waste allowance is applied and the total is rounded up to whole cans or pails.

interpret.title: How to interpret the results
items: Net area (per coat): actual square footage or square meters covered in one pass.
Total area to cover: net area multiplied by the number of coats.
Paint needed: total gallons or liters including waste allowance.
Containers needed: whole number of cans or pails rounded up.

items.title: 4 × 3 m bedroom at 2.5 m height (2 coats)
items.scenario: Walls only, 1 door and 1 window, 10 m²/L coverage and 0% waste.
items.calc: Walls = 35 m² − 3.25 m² openings = 31.75 m² × 2 coats = 63.5 m² ÷ 10 m²/L
items.result: Result: 6.35 L of paint (2 cans of 4 L).

items.title: 400 ft² wall area at 350 ft²/gal (1 coat)
items.scenario: Direct area mode, 1 coat, no openings, 0% waste.
items.result: Result: 1.143 gal of paint (2 cans of 1 gal).

faq.q: How much area does 1 gallon of paint cover?
faq.a: Standard interior latex paint typically covers 350 to 400 ft² per gallon per coat on smooth, primed drywall. Textured or porous surfaces may drop to 250–300 ft²/gal.

faq.q: How many coats of paint do I need?
faq.a: Two coats are standard for even color. Going from a dark color to a light one, or painting bare drywall without primer, may require 3 coats.

faq.q: Should I include the ceiling in the same calculation?
faq.a: Only if you are using the exact same paint for both walls and ceiling. If the ceiling uses flat white ceiling paint, calculate it separately in area mode.

faq.q: Why does the calculator round containers up?
faq.a: Because paint is sold in fixed cans or pails. Rounding up ensures you have enough to finish the final wall.

faq.q: What if I prefer not to subtract doors and windows?
faq.a: Leave both fields at 0. Keeping them at 0 gives you a small buffer for trim and future touch-ups.

flooring.metaTitle: Flooring Calculator Square Feet, Laminate & Vinyl | BuildCalc
flooring.metaDescription: Free square footage calculator for flooring, laminate flooring calculator, and vinyl flooring calculator. Estimate area, waste, tiles, and boxes.
flooring.intro: Use this square footage calculator for flooring—whether as a laminate flooring calculator, vinyl flooring calculator, or tile estimator—to calculate square feet or m², cutting waste, pieces, and full boxes.

fields.wasteHelp: Recommended: 10% for straight lay; 15% for diagonal or complex rooms.
fields.tileHelp: Tile or plank size. Leave empty if you only need the area.

guide.title: What it is for and how to use it
guide.purpose: This calculator estimates total square footage or square meters, individual tile/plank counts, and full boxes needed for floor or wall installations.
guide.howTitle: How to use it step by step
steps: Choose whether to enter room length and width or total area directly.
Set your waste percentage (10% for straight lay, 15% for diagonal patterns).
Enter the tile or plank dimensions (e.g., 60 × 60 cm or 12 × 24 in).
Select whether to calculate boxes by pieces per box or by area per box.

formula.title: Formula and calculation criteria
equations: Boxes = ceil(Pieces / Pieces_per_box) or ceil(Total area / Area_per_box)
formula.p1: Net area is multiplied by the waste factor to cover edge cuts, doorways and accidental breakage.
formula.p2: When tile dimensions are entered, single-piece area is computed and total area is divided by piece area, rounded up.
formula.p3: In pieces-per-box mode, total pieces are divided by pieces per box and rounded up.
formula.p4: In area-per-box mode (common for laminate and vinyl), total area is divided directly by box coverage.

interpret.title: How to interpret the results
items: Net area: exact room footprint before waste.
Total area (with waste): the area you should purchase.
Tiles / planks needed: whole number of individual pieces.
Boxes needed: full boxes rounded up so all material comes from the same dye lot.

items.title: 5 × 4 m room with 60 × 60 cm porcelain tiles
items.scenario: Straight lay with 10% waste and 4 tiles per box.
items.result: Result: 22.00 m² total, 62 tiles and 16 boxes.

faq.q: How much flooring waste should I add?
faq.a: Add 10% for straight installations in rectangular rooms, and 15% for diagonal layouts, herringbone patterns or rooms with many angles.

faq.q: Why should I order an extra box from the same batch?
faq.a: Tile shade and caliber can vary slightly between manufacturing batches. Keeping one extra box ensures matching replacements for future repairs.

faq.q: Does the calculator subtract grout lines?
faq.a: Nominal tile sizes already account for standard grout joints, so using nominal dimensions plus 10% waste is accurate.

faq.q: Does it work for laminate or vinyl plank flooring?
faq.a: Yes. Use 'By area covered per box' (standard on laminate/SPC packaging) or enter plank dimensions.

faq.q: What if my room is L-shaped?
faq.a: Split the room into two rectangles, add their areas together, and enter the sum in 'By total area' mode.

privacy.metaDescription: BuildCalc privacy policy: local browser storage, disabled analytics/ads, and how your data is handled.

sections.title: 1. Overview
sections.text: BuildCalc is a static construction calculator website. It requires no registration, has no user accounts, and does not collect personally identifiable information.

sections.title: 2. Browser-side calculations
sections.text: All measurements, quantities and results entered into the concrete, paint and flooring calculators are processed exclusively in your browser using JavaScript. No calculation data is sent to our servers or third parties.

sections.title: 3. Local preferences (localStorage)
sections.text: BuildCalc stores only two technical preferences in your browser's localStorage: 'bc.units' (to remember your metric or imperial choice) and 'bc.lang' (to remember your language choice when visiting the site root). You can clear these anytime in your browser settings.

sections.title: 4. Cookies
sections.text: BuildCalc does not set first-party cookies for its calculators. However, because Google Analytics 4 is active, Google may use third-party analytics cookies or identifiers to distinguish sessions and measure traffic.

sections.title: 5. Web analytics (Google Analytics 4)
sections.text: This site uses Google Analytics 4 to measure visits and improve site content and performance. Google may collect usage, browsing, approximate device data, and analytics cookies or identifiers. You can read Google's privacy policy at https://policies.google.com/privacy and opt out or limit analytics using Google's opt-out browser add-on (https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout) or by blocking cookies in your browser settings.

sections.title: 6. Advertising
sections.text: Advertising (such as Google AdSense) is currently disabled. If an ad provider is enabled in the future, this policy will be updated beforehand to explain cookies and consent choices.

sections.title: 7. Affiliate links
sections.text: There are currently no active affiliate links on the site. If sponsored or affiliate links are added in the future, they will be clearly labeled next to the relevant content.

sections.title: 8. Hosting and server logs
sections.text: This static site is hosted on Render. Like any web host, the hosting infrastructure may temporarily log basic technical request data (such as IP address, timestamp and requested URL) for security and availability.

sections.title: 9. External links
sections.text: This page may link to external websites (such as the project's public repository). BuildCalc does not control the privacy practices of third-party sites.

sections.title: 10. Children's privacy
sections.text: BuildCalc is not directed at children and does not knowingly collect personal information from any user.

sections.title: 11. Calculation accuracy
sections.text: All results are estimates for planning purposes. Always verify manufacturer specifications and consult a qualified professional before purchasing materials or building.

sections.title: 12. Your rights
sections.text: Because we do not store personal data on our own servers, there are no user profiles or personal databases tied to your visit. You can remove local preferences ('bc.units' and 'bc.lang') by clearing site data in your browser.

sections.title: 13. Changes to this policy
sections.text: We may update this policy when new features or services are introduced. The last-updated date is always shown at the top of this page.

sections.title: 14. Contact
sections.text: If you have questions or want to report an issue, you can open an issue on the public project repository at https://github.com/resktoff/Buildcalc-/issues.
